links.reason: Both deny worth to bare age: Puram 195's பயனில் மூப்பு and the saying's மறுபிறப்பு அறியாதது மூப்பு அன்று. The move from Death's binding (பிணிக்கும் காலை) to knowledge of the next birth is real, but the Puram poem is a பொருண்மொழிக் காஞ்சி warning, not a 'heroic' one, and it has no rebirth doctrine to transform; the pairing rests on a shared theme of worthless old age.

The pair shares the words பெருமை and சிறுமை, but in Kural 978 சிறுமை is the mean character who adorns himself (அணியும் தன்னை வியந்து), while in the saying it is low estate one must bear (சிறுமை நோனாதோன்). The humility reading joins two different senses of சிறுமை. list_adds describes the neighbouring line 68, not anything this one-item saying does.

The two verses do mirror each other (இருள்உலகம் சேராத ஆறு against நல்லுலகம் சேராதவர்), and கற்றாரைக் கைவிட்டு sits opposite சேர்தற்குச் செய்க பெருநூலை. But forsaking learned men isn't the same as study, and the closer mirror is speech (அருள்புரிந்து சொல்லுக against அலவலை). 'The book makes learning the hinge' claims more than two verses show.

Verse 71 counts ஈன்றெடுத்தல், சூல்புறஞ் செய்தல், குழவியை ஏன்றெடுத்தல் as பேரறம், and 73 spells out the same care in stages: கலங்காமைக் காத்தல், ஈற்றம், குழவி மருந்து, வெருட்டாமை, closing on அறம்பெருமை. The extension is real and specific, and the note describes both verses accurately.
links.text_issue: 73 line 2 இலங்காமை and the division விலங்காமைக் கோடல் are unclear.

links.reason: In Kar Narpathu 7 the rain brings him back (தரூஉம் ... மழை). His aim (நச்சியார்க்கு ஈதலும் நண்ணார்த் தெறுதலும்) is only why he went, not offered as a guarantee. The real tie is impermanence: அற்கா இயல்பிற்று செல்வம் and நில்லாமை உள்ளும் நெறிப்பாடு. But Kural 333 doesn't name giving (it says only அற்குப ஆங்கே செயல்); 'giving' is the commentator's. So the contrast in both teaches and list_adds, between derived and coordinate, rests on a gloss.

On the reading of சிற்றில் as a low birth-group, the saying assumes a rank that Naladiyar 195 calls சொல்லளவு அல்லால் பொருளில்லை, so a tension is defensible. But சிற்றில் may only mean a poor house, and the saying also reads rank from conduct (பெருமிதத்தின் அறிப), close to the quatrain's குலம் made by தவம் கல்வி ஆள்வினை. The note doesn't say which reading the conflict needs. list_adds rests on line 11, which isn't this verse.

Both define the same word: Acharakkovai 1 makes கல்வி one of the eight ஆசார வித்து, and Nanmanikkadigai 94 says ஆசாரம் என்பது கல்வி. Reducing ஆசாரம் to learning, against a book that goes on to ritual rules, is a real narrowing, so qualifies fits and teaches is specific.

links.text_issue: The colophon's வினைமுற்றிய தலைமகள் should be தலைமகன், who speaks to the charioteer (பாகற்கு).

links.reason: Both verses list what Death disregards (the six நோக்கான் in 23, the five அஞ்சான் in 22) and close on a book: பெரியார்நூல் as வாய்காப்பு in 23, பாவின்நூல் of the one who reached வீடு in 22. 23 adds occasions (மணம், மங்கலம், கணம்) to 22's defences, so it develops 22.

Kural 428 calls அஞ்சுவது அஞ்சாமை folly. Item 1, அஞ்சாமை அஞ்சுதி ஒன்றின், turns fear on fearlessness itself, so the object of fear becomes the man's own temper, as teaches says. It opens a four-item code (எஞ்சாமை, கோடாமை, நாடாதி), so list_adds holds.
links.text_issue: Line 1's division (அஞ்சாமை அஞ்சுதி ஒன்றின்) is not certain.

links.reason: Kural 322's பகுத்துண்டு returns in Elathi 44 as ஈத்துண்பான் and then as the reward பாத்துண்பான். The reward takes the shape of the act, a king who shares, which is specific and in the Tamil. Item 6 (வால்அடிசில் நையாதே ஈத்துண்பான்) carries the link, and the list does join speech (பொய்யான்), diet (புலால்உண்ணான்) and public work (வழிசீத்து).

verses.note: The five counted things are similes for the melting heart of the giver (ஒன்றுபோல் உள்நெகிழ்ந்து ஈயின்), not five acts.
கரப்புச்சொல் is named twice (absent from the learned, present in the base), so items 2 and 4 share a word.
The reward is kingship (மண் ஆளும்), but the counsel (heeding elders, keeping servants, giving food) is to the householder; மாறான் in line 4 is read as qualifying the reward.
Norm given for கற்பு as the period's rule of marital fidelity; the verse doesn't name a woman, so this is a judgment call.
The count word names the four outward practices to be given up; the fifth item is the restraint of the five (ஐந்தடக்கு), giving five in all; lines 1-2 are obscure.

The five are outward marks of renunciants, which the verse sets against the claim that in Kali the householder's life is the true one; norm left null because it judges ascetic display rather than stating a purity rule.
Seven words name recipients; துறவாதார் துப்பிலார் is taken as one class to give six, but seven is possible.
The invocation counsels no one; domain all is a default, and the four items are the likenesses of Mayavan's face, discus, eye and colour.
No counted list: மூன்று ஐந்து ஏழ் number births before release, not things, so no items are given.
Domain ascetic because the verse describes the state of release (உயர்கதி), the renouncer's goal.
Lines 3-4 are taken as one item (wealth that comes to the worthy, if unending); counting மாண்புடையார்ச் சேரும் apart would give four.
நின்ற நிலைகல்வி is taken as one item to fit ஆறும்; the beauties are assigned to மறையின் வழிவந்தார், a birth term, hence caste.
The items mix the faster, the host and the one who keeps from others' houses, so all is given; the division is uncertain.
Lines 3-4 are obscure; the diet norm rests on ஊன் ஆரத் தொடங்கானேல் (not beginning to eat flesh).
வையார் (revile or keep) is read with both பெண் and மன், giving six; the gender norm rests on வரைவில்லாப் பெண்.
Choosing an auspicious day for marriage (தோள்கூட்டல்) is a rule of the hours, but its audience is the householder arranging a marriage.
The saying runs over two lines; line 1 only sets the scope (ஆர்கலி யுலகத்து மக்கட் கெல்லாம்).
குலஞ்சிதைக்குங் கூடார்கண் கூடி விடின் may be a rule on joining with those of another kind, which would be caste; it is left null because கூடார் is more plainly 'foes, those not in accord'.
